slot.brief: Given magnetic flux through a coil varying with time as a polynomial, use Faraday's law to find the induced emf at a given instant.

stem: The magnetic flux through each turn of a $4$-turn coil varies as $\bigl(2t^2-3t+5\bigr)$ mWb, where $t$ is in seconds. The magnitude of the induced emf at $t=2$ s is

verdicts.working: By Faraday’s law, |ε| = N|dΦ/dt|. At t = 2 s, dΦ/dt = (4t − 3) = 5 mWb/s, so |ε| = 4 × 5 = 20 mV.

working:
$e=-N\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}$
$\left|e\right|=4\left|(4t-3)\right|_{t=2}\text{ mWb s}^{-1}$
$=4(5)\text{ mV}=20\text{ mV}$

Independent check: By Faraday’s law, |ε| = N|dΦ/dt|. At t = 2 s, dΦ/dt = (4t − 3) = 5 mWb/s, so |ε| = 4 × 5 = 20 mV.
solution:
By Faraday’s law, $|e|=N\left|\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}\right|$. Since $\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}=4t-3$, at $t=2\,\text{s}$:
$$|e|=4|4(2)-3|\,\text{mWb s}^{-1}=20\,\text{mV}$$
